preamble: Palatalization of the voiceless velar stop [k] to the voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕ] before front vowels and [j]. In Mandarin, Middle Chinese velars before high front vowels and medial -j- merged with the alveolar sibilants into the alveolo-palatal series written j/q/x in Pinyin, so that 家 Middle Chinese kae is Mandarin jiā [tɕi̯ä], while Cantonese keeps [k] (gaa1). The same outcome arose independently in Finland Swedish, where historical /k/ before front vowels is the affricate [tɕ] (Sweden Swedish has the fricative [ɕ]), and in Southern Gyeongsang Korean, where ki is pronounced [tɕi].

examples.note: Sweden Swedish /²ɕʏrka/ has a fricative; Finland Swedish keeps the affricate stage except in some Åland dialects.
Dialectal palatalization of ki/ky to [tɕ] (Korean ㅈ), e.g. also 귤 "tangerine" > jul.
